title: Nine Parts Hedge
subtitle: 边界与界限 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 边界与界限（社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：边界与界限（社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：boundary　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 boundary 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my mother was sent to mark ① a boundary she could not cross, and she said the crossing was the whole of the lesson. The ② boundary, meaning the line and not the field, was six miles long and was walked by whoever came last; a boundary, she said, is the only thing in a register that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ boundary in that register had the same hedge, and the ④ boundary at the east, meaning the one the surveyor walked and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever marked properly. A boundary, my grandmother said, is nine parts hedge and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the hedge is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ boundary was the whole of the law, meaning the law it carried and not the line. The ⑥ boundary, meaning the law and not any of that, is the only thing in a parish that everybody accepts and nobody questions; a boundary, he said, is either something you mark or the only word that means both a line and a law. She said the law is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ boundary had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the hedge. The ⑧ boundary of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was six miles of hedge and eleven years of walking; a boundary, she said, is either the one at the east or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ boundary I remember is the one at the east, which was agreed in 1974 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ boundary, my grandmother said in 1983, is the only thing that improves by being agreed; every boundary, she said, is a law that has agreed to look like a line. She said the law was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 边界（指那条线本身，与田地相对）
C. 固定搭配：mark a boundary 标出一条界线
D. n. 边界（指登记簿上每一条）
E. n. 边界（指东面那一条）
F. n. 界限；规则（抽象：与那条线相对）
G. n. 那条法律、那份规矩（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a boundary she could not cross
The boundary, meaning the line and not the field
boundary was the whole of the law
the boundary had become a photograph in a report
The boundary of the whole thing
A boundary, my grandmother said in 1983

answers.why: mark a boundary 意为“标出一条界线”，1950 年母亲被派去标一条她跨不过去的界线。
boundary 意为“边界”，指那条线本身而不是田地，长六英里，由最后走的人走完。
boundary 指登记簿上每一条边界，每一条都依着同一道树篱。
boundary 指东面那一条（测量员走的那一条），是唯一有人认真标出的。
boundary 意为“界限、规则”，与那条线相对，父亲说 boundary 就是那条法律的全部。
boundary 为抽象用法，指那条法律、那份规矩本身，是教区里人人都接受、却没人质疑的东西。
boundary 意为“边界、分界线”，到 1968 年这条 boundary 成了报告里的一张照片。
boundary 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是六英里的树篱和十一年的行走。
boundary 意为“边界”，我记得的是东面那一条，1974 年被大家认可，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
boundary 为抽象总称，祖母说界限是唯一会因为被大家认可而变好的东西。
